title: Premium and minimal: choose the visual world
question: A safer, premium-minimal lineup. Pick one, take the category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: Exhibition Catalogue
options.lineage: museum exhibition catalogues and Swiss editorial layout
options.thesis: The conference presented like a gallery catalogue: real photographs of past editions, generous white space, precise type, every image captioned with its edition.
options.viewport: Large light-weight headline and Submit/Register on the left, one tall photograph from the 3rd ICSIFT on the right, a ruled fact line below: dates, city, indexing, credit.
options.risk: The most familiar of the three: premium-minimal is where many polished sites land, so it relies on craft rather than a concept.

options.label: Herbarium Sheet
options.lineage: botanical herbarium sheets and accession labels
options.thesis: Each section is a mounted specimen sheet: one image, a precise accession label of facts, deep botanical green as the only colour.
options.viewport: A white sheet mounted on pale grey-green: a tall photograph as the specimen, the title and two actions beside it, an accession label holding date, city and indexing.
options.risk: Can feel like a museum archive if the labels are fussy; the metaphor must stay quiet.

options.label: Printed Programme
options.thesis: The site as the conference's printed programme: a deep green cover beside a clean, ruled schedule page.
options.viewport: Green cover half with title and actions; white page half listing Day 1, Day 2, indexing and credit as ruled rows.
options.risk: Split-half layout can read as a standard two-column template.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The conference site as Nature Conferences, TED and the World Economic Forum events pages ship it, at their craft level.
canonCard.viewport: Photo hero with title, dates, venue and two buttons, then highlights, dates, speakers.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
